title: Accounts payable automation: what does it cost, what needs a person?
description: 13 accounts payable (AP) automation and invoice-capture tools checked, with prices where they exist. Reading invoices is solved; exceptions and fraud are not.
summary: OCR only turns an invoice into text; AI accounts payable (AP) automation also codes it, matches it to the purchase order (PO) and routes it for approval[^27][^21]. Reading costs cents[^10][^11]. Money leaks in two places: exceptions, about 1 invoice in 5[^8], and fake bank-change requests[^12].
humanRole: AP specialist: clears the exceptions, about 1 invoice in 5, and makes the call the tool only flags.[^8][^1] Keep three-way match (invoice, PO and receipt agree) on; Washington's state auditor says it "should not be eliminated in order to save time."[^49]

Supplier-list owner, not the paying clerk: adds suppliers and approves any bank-detail change.[^48][^50] Each change gets a call-back on a number already on file, never one from the request.[^50][^12]

AP manager or treasury: releases payment, and is never the person who entered the invoice.[^48][^49] Federal standards split approving, recording and paying so no one person controls a payment; small teams can use other checks instead.[^51][^48]

Controller: owns fraud monitoring on ACH (US bank-transfer) payments. Since June 2026, Nacha, which runs ACH, requires every business that sends ACH payments to have risk-based fraud checks, covering vendor impersonation.[^52][^53]
teamAfter: Exceptions become the main job. Ardent calls them the biggest single reason AP costs are not lower, and they hit about 1 invoice in 5.[^1][^8]

Fewer "where's my payment?" calls: AP staff spend 21.9% to 29.4% of their time on supplier questions.[^1][^56] Ardent's top-performing teams spend about half as much, and exceptions cause much of it.[^1]
Fraud checks: most AP teams already help prevent fraud, 72% heavily and 79% at least moderately.[^56][^55] Ardent calls AP "often the last line of defense against fraud."[^55]

Analysis: BLS expects clerks to take on "a more analytical and advisory role" as software automates routine tasks.[^54] Among US firms using AI, 66% use it only to help staff; 2% saw AI-related employment fall.[^57]
verdict: The money leaks in exceptions: about 1 invoice in 5 needs a person.[^8][^1]
Buy an AP suite such as BILL, Ramp or Tipalti to run approvals and payments[^5][^6].
Build AI only for the gaps, such as exception triage and holds on bank-detail changes[^8][^12].
Benchmark any tool on 50 of your own invoices: look-alike tables fooled 7 of 10 tools in our test.[^9][^61]
Treat any "new bank account" request as fraud until you call the supplier back on a number already on file.[^50][^12]

ownData.title: How much does accounts payable (AP) automation cost?
ownData.intro: Listed AP suite prices start at free (Ramp), $49 per user a month (BILL) and $99 a month (Tipalti); the other 6 of 9 full suites publish no price[^6][^5][^7][^18][^19][^21][^23][^24][^26]. Budget for add-ons on top, such as matching and per-invoice or per-payment fees[^6][^16][^17][^7]. We read all 13 pricing pages below (9 suites, 3 capture tools and QuickBooks), and 7 give no list price for a paid plan[^18][^19][^21][^23][^24][^26][^31].
rows: $49, $65 or $89 per user a month; Enterprise by quote[^5]
QuickBooks and Xero sync from Team; NetSuite and Intacct only on Enterprise[^5]
Free; Plus $15 per user a month plus a platform fee[^6]
3-way match (invoice, PO and receipt agree) needs Plus or a paid Procurement add-on; ACH and wires carry per-payment fees[^6][^16][^17]
Per-invoice and per-payment fees on top, amounts not published[^7]
PO matching is semi-automated unless you add its AI agent[^18]
Built for mid-market firms; price only through a demo[^19]
Priced per customer by volume, users and features[^21]
Payments are a paid add-on; fraud checks only on the top plan[^23]
Some new approval and PO-matching features reach only US and Nordic customers[^28]
$100 a month for 100 credits after $50 of free credit[^30]
Site estimates under $2 an invoice; Starter capped at 3 users[^30]
Free 14-day trial up to 1,000 pages; then by quote[^31]
Setup fees extra; unused monthly credits do not roll over[^31]
ownData.note: Source: each vendor's pricing page, read 26 November 2026[^5][^6][^7][^18][^19][^21][^23][^24][^26][^29][^30][^31][^32]. 'Full AP' means capture, approvals and payment in one product. Prices are US list prices before discounts.

example.input: A two-page PDF invoice emailed by a supplier, with a purchase order number and a note that the bank account has changed.
example.output: Supplier, invoice number, date, lines, tax and total, matched to the purchase order and receipt and coded to the right accounts. Held for a person to check, because the bank details differ from the supplier record.

recipes.name: 1. Buy the suite and switch on its AI
flow: Suppliers email invoices to the AP inbox
Suite reads and codes them; AP clerk checks the flagged ones
Suite matches each invoice to the PO and the receipt that Receiving logged
Budget owner approves; Controller approves over limit
AP manager or treasury releases payment; the approver can't release it
Suite syncs to your accounting system (ERP)
recipes.cost: BILL costs $49 to $89 per user a month[^5]. Ramp is free, or $15 per user a month plus a platform fee[^6]; Tipalti starts at $99 a month plus fees[^7].

recipes.name: 2. Add an AI check where your suite falls short
recipes.when: You already have AP software but exceptions and fraud attempts still get through.
flow: New invoice lands in the AP inbox
AI reads it and shows where on the page each value came from
AI compares it with the PO, the receipt that Receiving logged and the supplier record
AI flags any bank-detail change and holds the payment
The person who owns the supplier list, not the paying clerk, calls the supplier back on a number already on file.[^50][^12]
AP clerk releases it to approval; Controller approves over limit
recipes.cost: Reading an invoice costs cents with a cloud invoice reader[^10][^11], against a median $6.00 to an average $9.90 to process one invoice today[^2][^8]. The real cost is building and owning the hold rules; we quote that per job and don't publish a price here.

recipes.name: 3. Capture only, into your own ERP
recipes.when: High volume of standard invoices and an ERP that already handles approvals and payment.
flow: AP clerk scans paper invoices or forwards the PDFs
Capture tool or cloud invoice parser reads them
If AI is unsure, it reads again
AP clerk checks what is still unsure
AP clerk posts to the ERP
recipes.cost: Amazon Textract reads invoices for $10 per 1,000 pages[^10]; Google charges $0.10 per invoice of up to 10 pages[^11]; Rossum starts at $18,000 a year[^29].

rules.name: Germany: B2B e-invoicing
rules.what: All businesses must be able to receive EN 16931 e-invoices since 1 Jan 2025. Larger firms must issue them from 2027 and nearly all from 2028[^36][^37][^42].

rules.name: France: B2B e-invoicing
rules.what: Every business must be able to receive e-invoices; large and mid-size firms must issue them. Small firms issue from 1 Sep 2027[^38][^39]. A scan or an ordinary PDF sent by email no longer counts as an e-invoice[^40].

rules.name: United States
rules.what: No federal or state B2B e-invoicing mandate[^43]. A voluntary network, DBNAlliance, grew out of an industry pilot the Federal Reserve supported[^44][^43].

howToTest: Record your before numbers first: cost per invoice, exception rate, straight-through rate and days per invoice. Multiply cost per invoice by your monthly volume to get your unit's AP cost today.
Compare your baseline with the benchmark figures on this page: 19.9% exceptions, 38.3% straight through and 11.6 days per invoice[^8].
For two weeks, log the minutes your team spends on each exception. That gives you your own cost of an exception.
Pull 50 recent invoices from one entity or one AP inbox, including at least 10 past exceptions. Include credit notes, multi-page invoices, foreign ones and the worst scans.
Write down the right supplier, number, date, total, tax and PO for each before any tool reads them.
Run each tool on the same set. Count wrong values apart from blanks: a wrong total is worse than a missing one.
Add three invoices that change a supplier's bank details, and check each tool holds them.
Add one invoice you already paid, resubmitted, and check each tool flags it as a duplicate.

Measure how many invoices go straight through, how many reach your team as exceptions, and the cost per invoice including add-ons. Multiply the change in cost per invoice by your monthly volume to get the saving in dollars.

buyVsBuild.buy: Buy for the workflow: inbox, approvals, payments, ERP sync and an audit trail. Suites already sell all of this[^5][^6][^7], and you do not want to own payments.
buyVsBuild.build: Build only the checks your suite misses: exception triage, fraud holds, duplicate-invoice checks[^22], odd document types or your own coding rules. Start with one entity or one AP inbox, and keep the rest on today's process until the benchmark holds. Exceptions still hit about one invoice in five[^8], so these checks flag what your AP team should look at; the decision stays with a person.

watchOuts: The price you see is rarely the price you pay. Matching, payments, more entities and ERP sync are often add-ons[^5][^16][^7][^23].

Payment fraud rides on invoices[^12][^13]: 74% of US organizations experienced business email compromise in 2025, the AFP found[^4][^15]. Check any change to bank details by calling the supplier on a number already on file.[^50][^12]
A tool that reads the subtotal as the total looks right at a glance. In our benchmark, 7 of 10 tools picked the wrong one of two look-alike tables[^9].

faq.a: Software that reads supplier invoices, codes them, matches them to the purchase order and routes them for approval and payment.[^19][^27] AI does the reading and suggests the coding; your AP team still clears exceptions and approves payments.[^8][^48]

faq.q: How much does AP automation cost?
faq.a: Listed AP automation prices start at free (Ramp), $49 per user a month (BILL) and $99 a month (Tipalti).[^6][^5][^7] Those are the only 3 of the 9 full AP suites we checked that publish a price; the rest quote after a demo, and add-ons such as matching and payment fees cost extra.[^18][^19][^16][^17]

No, AI changes the accounts payable job more than it removes it. Among US firms using AI, 66% use it only to help staff, and 2% saw AI-related employment fall.[^57] BLS still projects bookkeeping and accounting clerk jobs to fall 6% by 2035, with about 144,100 openings a year.[^54]

faq.q: How long does AP automation take to set up?
faq.a: Vendors say weeks, not months: AvidXchange says many customers are live in as little as six weeks; Ramp says 2 to 12.[^19][^58] Ramp says most of that time goes to cleaning supplier data and settling who approves what.[^58] Tipalti says technical setup takes days, but company checks and account setup can take several weeks.[^59]

faq.q: Can I trust AP automation accuracy claims?
faq.a: Only after a test on your own invoices.[^61] In a Fraunhofer study, the best model got 96.5% of fields right on clean invoices but 87.5% on scanned receipts.[^60] In our own test, two look-alike tables fooled 7 of 10 tools.[^9]

offer.heading: Invoices still stuck in exceptions? Get a free diagnostic
offer.body: Tell us your AP tool, your monthly invoice count and where invoices get stuck. In 30 minutes you learn which suite fits and whether a custom check (recipe 2) pays at your volume. You leave with the first step and a before-and-after measure in writing, with no sales pitch.

reviews.notes: Couldn't see who does what from the top, and the before-and-after measure was called a baseline. On this page now leads with who decides, approves and releases payment, follows the page order and links the cost and setup-time answers. The first test step now says these are your before numbers.

Tripped on ACH, Nacha and Best-in-Class. ACH is now defined as US bank transfers, Nacha as the body that runs it, and Best-in-Class as Ardent's top-performing teams. Three-way match is defined where it first appears, and the setup-time answer says company checks instead of due diligence.

Asked whether one unit can pilot first and what it does to the unit's cost. The test now pulls its 50 invoices from one entity or one AP inbox, and the last step turns the change in cost per invoice into dollars a month. The setup-time answer gives the vendors' week ranges, marked as their claims.

The head of AP and controller checked the controls against the sources. The bottom line's call-back now says a number already on file, matching the state auditor and FBI, and the recipe and watch-out say the same. The payment-release role now notes that small teams can use other checks when they can't split duties.

Steve found the price answer and the jobs answer where he would look, but the offer told him to forward the follow-up to his CEO, which is him. The offer now asks for his monthly invoice count and promises the first step and a before-and-after measure in writing, with no sales pitch.
